pr.title: feat(sleep): Sleep Image Order setting — Random or In Order
pr.body:
## Summary

* **Goal:** let custom sleep images play like a slideshow instead of a shuffle.
* **What changes:** a new Display setting, **Sleep Image Order**:
  * **Random** (default) — the existing shuffle, unchanged.
  * **In Order** — each sleep shows the next valid image after the last one shown, in path order across `/.sleep` and `/sleep`, wrapping to the first.
* The folders are rescanned on every sleep, so added and removed images take effect at once. One directory pass, no file-name list in RAM; the last shown path lives in `/.crosspoint/sleep_last.txt`. `/sleep.bmp` keeps its priority over the folders.

![Sleep Image Order: In Order — four sleeps in a row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MikalaiKryvusha/crosspoint-reader/pr-assets/06-sleep-order/sleep-in-order.png)

*Simulator, three test images in `/sleep`, four sleeps in a row.*

## Scope Check

- [x] I have read SCOPE.md and ROADMAP.md.
- [x] This PR is **not** a new built-in theme.
- [x] This PR is **not** a new external network connector.
- [x] This PR is **not** an interactive app, writing tool, RSS/news/browser, media playback, or PDF feature.
- [x] The stock firmware does not already handle this well, **and** no other popular CrossPoint fork already does.
- [x] This PR does not touch `freeink-sdk/`, `lib/hal/`, the bootloader, OTA, or recovery code.

## Additional Context

* `pio run -e x4pro` is green; all 893 host tests pass.
* New strings: English and Russian; other languages fall back to English.
* The same ordering has been on my X4 Pro build for a while.

---

### AI Usage

Did you use AI tools to help write this code? _**YES**_ — Claude (Anthropic) wrote the change under my direction; I reviewed it.

Personally, I don't think people care about the order. 

We recently merged PR which make the randomness much better - which was a thing we got complains about.

> Personally, I don't think people care about the order.
> 
> We recently merged PR which make the randomness much better - which was a thing we got complains about.

Randomization can provide a delightful element of surprise—you never know which photo from your collection will appear as the screensaver each time the device is locked. If the device is used by a loved one and the collection includes family photos from various years, this randomization becomes a truly pleasant feature. Furthermore, "smart" randomization ensures that the same photo isn't shown twice in a row.

Supported by static analysis
Script executed: ```bash rg -n 'deep_sleep|deepSleep|esp_restart|powerOff|shutdown|SleepActivity|RTC_DATA_ATTR|RTC_NOINIT_ATTR' src lib/hal sed -n '1,220p' src/activities/boot_sleep/SleepActivity.cpp ``` Repository: crosspoint-reader/crosspoint-reader Length of output: 13525 ---
**A failed `sleep_last.txt` write can repeat the same sleep image.** In sequential mode, `writeFile` failure at lines 542-545 logs the error and still returns `true`. The next sleep reads the cursor from disk. A missing or empty cursor selects the first image again. An unchanged cursor selects the same successor again. While the write keeps failing, sleeps can repeat the same image. Keeping the selected path in a RAM variable does not prevent this. Sleep enters deep sleep, and wake restarts the firmware, so ordinary RAM is cleared before the next selection. A fix needs state that survives deep sleep, such as RTC memory. It also needs a rule for choosing between that state and the disk cursor when both exist.
